description: * I've created a Github repo with a Dockerfile that reproduces some of what I see locally: https://github.com/trevorld/textshaping_issue_76 * On Linux I'm observing some possible bugs when I draw `textGrob()` in `{ragg}` or `marquee_grob()` in `{ragg}` or Cairo devices when I have some text following a glyph that isn't in the requested font that has both an emoji form and a non-emoji form. * I don't observe any such problem with `textGrob()` in Cairo devices. In the Docker container the following example ```r library("grDevices") library("grid") text_no_fallback <- "Double Pinochle (SQ,SQ,DJ,DJ) = 300" text_yes_fallback <- "Double Pinochle (\u2660\ufe0eQ,\u2660\ufe0eQ,\u2662\ufe0eJ,\u2662\ufe0eJ) = 300" font <- "Carlito" gp <- gpar(fontfamily = font, fontsize = 18) # `textGrob()` ragg::agg_png("textGrob_ragg.png") grid.text(text_yes_fallback, y = 0.75, gp = gp) grid.text(text_no_fallback, y = 0.25, gp = gp) dev.off() |> invisible() cairo_pdf("textGrob_cairo.pdf", width = 6.67, height = 6.67) grid.text(text_yes_fallback, y = 0.75, gp = gp) grid.text(text_no_fallback, y = 0.25, gp = gp) dev.off() |> invisible() ``` gives the following in {ragg}: but instead gives the following in a Cairo-device: * I do note that the request to select a non-emoji form of the Spades playing card suit glyph using `U+FE0E` (Variation Selector 15: Text-mode) i.e. `\u2660\ufe0e` seems to work in the Cairo device but not in {ragg}. * The Spades playing card suit does not seem to be in the requested Carlito font so both devices are resorting to a form of font fallback. * After performing font fallback on the Spades glyph I observe that the {ragg} examples (and {marquee} examples on other graphics devices) don't seem to "return" back to the original requested font even for glyphs it contains like "= 300". * I also observe problems if I try to use a `marquee_grob()` instead of `textGrob()` but locally I can get something that looks okay if I wrap the Spades suit glyph with a span like `{.black \u2660\ufe0e}` instead of just `\u2660\ufe0e`).

title: Conflict with ggplot2 and Arabic & Hindi
description:
A workaround is necessary to get `ggplot2` to work with Arabic and Hindi when `flextable` is loaded. (Issue is also discussed here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79324809/conflict-between-flextable-ggplot2-and-arabic-hindi). I narrowed the problem down to `textshaping`, which is a dependent of `ragg`, which is a dependent of `officer`, which is a dependent of `flextable`. Here's an example that also includes English and Russian to show that things work fine with those:

```
library(dplyr) # data management
library(flextable) # used elsewhere in application
library(ggplot2) # chart

datDf <- tibble(En = c("Orange","Purple"),
                Ru = c("оранжевый","Пурпурный"),
                Hi = c("नारंगी","जामुनी"),
                Ar = c("برتقالي","بنفسجي"), # R handles the direction change
                xMin = c(1,2),
                xMax = c(3,4)) %>%
  # keep rows in order for plot
  mutate(across(c(En,Ru,Hi,Ar), ~factor(.x, levels=rev(.x)))) 

plotFun <- function(labLang){
  # x-axis labels
  xTiks <- switch(deparse(substitute(labLang)),
                  En = c("1.0\nAlmost Never",
                         "2.0\nRarely",
                         "3.0\nSometimes",
                         "4.0\nOften",
                         "5.0\nAlmost Always"),
                  Ru = c("1.0\nПочти никогда",
                         "2.0\nРедко",
                         "3.0\nИногда",
                         "4.0\nЧасто",
                         "5.0\nПочти всегда"),
                  Hi = c("1.0\nलगभग कभी नही",
                         "2.0\nशायद ही कभी",
                         "3.0\nकभी-कभी",
                         "4.0\nअक्सर",
                         "5.0\nलगभग हमेशा"),
                  Ar = c("1.0\nتقريبًا لا على الإطلاق",
                         "2.0\nنادرًا",
                         "3.0\nفي بعض الأحيان",
                         "4.0\nغالبًا",
                         "5.0\nتقريبًا دائمًا")
                  )
  plt1 <- ggplot(datDf, aes(y={{labLang}}, xmin=xMin, xmax=xMax)) +
    geom_linerange()
  plt2 <- if (deparse(substitute(labLang)) == "Ar") {
    # handle right-to-left for Arabic
    plt1 +
      scale_x_reverse(labels=xTiks, limits=c(5,1)) +
      scale_y_discrete(position="right")
  } else {
    plt1 +
      scale_x_continuous(labels=xTiks, limits=c(1,5))
  }
  return(plt2)
}

plotFun(En) # English
plotFun(Ru) # Russian
plotFun(Hi) # Hindi
plotFun(Ar) # Arabic
```

English output (works fine):

![English](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e4de664-9581-4bfb-9c1b-81eabe9fadb9)

Russian output (works fine):
![Russian](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d355934-9367-4e8b-bc72-77c40883d52b)

Hindi output (text is removed):
![Hindi2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/029e7a7d-4934-49b1-8419-5da37ce38124)

The Arabic plot doesn't render at all.

Using `unloadNamespace("textshaping")` before running the plot functions didn't work, but using `pkgload::unload("textshaping")` _did_ work, and the plots render as expected.

Hindi:
![Hindi1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff71ce3c-46cc-47b9-9eee-b994702259a5)

Arabic:
![Arabic](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bc7e6d3-5212-4953-808c-70a4139aeca7)

Hindi and Arabic seem to render fine when actually using them in a `flextable` (as far as I can tell - I still need to confirm with my translators), so the issue is thus far limited to `ggplot2`. The `pkgload::unload` workaround serves me fine at the moment, but thought y'all might like to know something is up.

title: Unicode text fails after attaching ragg
description:
Attaching the `ragg` package prevents one from using unicode characters in base `plot()` and `ggplot()`, as any string with unicode will be blank. However, printing a plot (with either `plot()` or `ggplot()`) before attaching ragg fixes the issue:

```{r}
library('ragg')
plot(1, xlab = '\U1D53C doesn\'t work')
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(1, 1)) +
  ggplot2::xlab('\U1D53C doesn\'t work')

# restart R (Ctrl + Shift + F10)

plot(1, xlab = '\U1D53C')
library('ragg')
plot(1, xlab = '\U1D53C now works')
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(1, 1)) +
  ggplot2::xlab('\U1D53C now works')

# restart R (Ctrl + Shift + F10)

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(1, 1)) +
  ggplot2::xlab('\U1D53C')
library('ragg')
plot(1, xlab = '\U1D53C now works')
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(1, 1)) +
  ggplot2::xlab('\U1D53C now works')
```

I am using `R` 4.2.1, RStudio 2022.07.1+554 "Spotted Wakerobin", and `ragg` 1.2.3 on Windows 10.

title: Conflict with base-R's file.choose()
description:
There seems to be a conflict with base-R's file.choose() when loading 'ragg' on Windows 10.
```
library(ragg)
file.choose()
```
leads to a "Select files" dialog where all fonts have disappeared.
The issue also exists for choose.files() and choose.dir() from the utils-package.

Interestingly, if executing from a fresh session:
```
file.choose()
library(ragg)
file.choose()
```
the fonts are shown correctly, indicating that calling file.choose() caches the fonts before the conflict with 'ragg'.

Any help with this issue would be appreciated.

description:

title: Retrieving glyphs with `shape_text()`
description:
Hello Thomas and team,

Summarising the issue below: it would be wonderful if the `shape_text()` function could return unicode glyphs or codepoints.

I think the `shape_text()` function is great for its support for BiDi text and character composition, so thank you so much for bringing the Harfbuzz and Fridibi libraries to the R ecosystem! It has been very helpful for a ggplot2 extension we've been working on.

Currently, the `shape_text()` function does not return the glyphs as code points or unicode, but does helpfully return an index to the font file. Using a workaround, we can use `systemfonts::glyph_info()` to query all indices of a font and reconstruct from there. This works if the font supports the glyphs that we want, but does not work in all cases because we cannot enjoy font fallback in this way.

``` r
library(textshaping)

# Example Japanese text taken from here: https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2021/02/modern-text-features/#font-fallback
x <- shape_text("Test \u3053\u306e\u65E5\u672C\u8A9E\u3067\u3059", family = "Arial")

# Querying most of unicode space
glyphs <- systemfonts::glyph_info(
  intToUtf8(1:64000, multiple = TRUE), family = "Arial"
)

# Translating font indices back to glyphs
i <- match(x$shape$index, glyphs$index)
do.call(paste0, list(glyphs$glyph[i], collapse = ""))
#> [1] "Test \001\001\001\001\001\001\001"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-12-10 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

We have tried various other methods such as `strsplit()`'ing the `metrics$string` output, but this becomes hairy when the string contains compound characters. Even using `stringi::stri_split_boundaries(..., type = "character")` does not always return the same lengths of strings as there are rows in the `shape` output.

So my question is this: what is a reliable method to retrieve (clusters of) glyphs parallel to the rows of the `shape` output? If there isn't any, please feel free to consider this issue a feature request instead.

Thanks for reading!

title: {ragg} crashes if the font doesn't contain the unicode character
description:
We, at JASP, ran into this [issue](https://github.com/jasp-stats/INTERNAL-jasp/issues/1540) where `ragg` crashes if our dataset contains a specific character which is not supported by the font. This is a common issues I guess, but I was hopping that we get a placeholder instead of full on crash. I'm wondering if anyone has experienced something like this, and if there is any workaround for it.

The following example only works with a handful of fonts, Arial, Times, and Tahoma. The culprit is this  Ӻ, [Cyrillic Capital (and Small) Letter Ghe with stroke and hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Unicode_characters) character which is not supported by many fonts. If you remove this character, then the plot will be generated with no issue. 

```r
# Removing the Ӻ from the string
# dd[30, "unicode"] <- "₢_Ἁ__ט_ሜ_ழ_क़_ᚽ_ㄸ"
# dd[31, "unicode"] <- "₣_ἅ__טּ_ም_ள_ख_ᚾ_ﾨ"

plt <- ggplot2::ggplot(dd, ggplot2::aes(x = unicode)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(stat = "count")

plot(plt)

ragg::agg_png("plotje.png")
plot(plt)
dev.off()
```

Is there a way to stop `ragg` from crashing the R session, or patch it such that it returns a placeholder instead of the missing character?

title: arm64 macos 11 configure tweaks
description:
as per the twitter thread, I ended up having to tweak `PKG_CONFIG_NAME`, `PKG_BREW_NAME`, and `PKG_LIBS`:

```
# Library settings
PKG_CONFIG_NAME="harfbuzz freetype2 fribidi png"
PKG_DEB_NAME="libharfbuzz-dev libfribidi-dev"
PKG_RPM_NAME="harfbuzz-devel fribidi-devel"
PKG_CSW_NAME="libharfbuzz_dev libfribidi_dev"
PKG_BREW_NAME="harfbuzz fribidi libpng"
PKG_TEST_HEADER="#include <hb-ft.h>"
PKG_LIBS="-lfreetype -lharfbuzz -lfribidi -lpng"
```

as well as:

```
# Use pkg-config if available
if [ "`command -v pkg-config`" ]; then
  PKGCONFIG_CFLAGS="`/opt/homebrew/bin/pkg-config --cflags --silence-errors ${PKG_CONFIG_NAME}`"
  PKGCONFIG_LIBS="`/opt/homebrew/bin/pkg-config --libs ${PKG_CONFIG_NAME}`"
fi
```

to get it to compile.

Compilation also requires a full Xcode installation.
